title: Understand computer vision at work · Level 3
slo: Identify what computer vision does and match it to common workplace uses.

exercises.question_text: What does computer vision help machines understand?

options.text: Visual information from images and video
options.rationale: This is correct. Computer vision interprets images, video, and camera feeds.
This is incorrect. Spoken audio is not visual input.
options.better_fit: Audio analysis fits tasks based on speech or sound recordings.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. Creating an image differs from interpreting one.
options.better_fit: Image generation fits creating visuals from written prompts.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. Spreadsheets do not supply visual scene information.
options.better_fit: Tabular-data analysis fits structured numerical records.

exercises.question_text: Retail shelf monitoring helps radiologists find possible fractures in CT scans.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A store task would be confused with a radiology task.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Retail shelf monitoring detects out-of-stock or misplaced store products.

exercises.question_text: Which tasks can computer vision models perform? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. Identifying objects is a common vision task.
This is correct. Vision models can recognize patterns in visual data.
This is correct. Vision models can extract or recognize visible text.
This is incorrect. Video generation creates content instead of analyzing input.
options.better_fit: Video generation fits producing a new video clip.

exercises.explanation: Correct—computer vision can identify, recognize, and read visual content.

exercises.question_text: Recognizing road signs, lane markings, pedestrians, and other vehicles supports safe navigation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A vehicle could navigate with less critical road information.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Recognizing signs, lanes, pedestrians, and vehicles supports safe navigation.

exercises.explanation: Correct—these visual details support informed road decisions.

exercises.question_text: Dividing an image into meaningful regions for detailed analysis is image ___.

parts.text: Dividing an image into meaningful regions for detailed analysis is image

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The image-area process would be mislabeled.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use segmentation for dividing regions; use detection for locating objects.

exercises.explanation: Image segmentation divides an image into meaningful regions or object areas.

exercises.question_text: A transport team must choose a vision solution for safe decisions in changing road environments. Which reasons support autonomous vehicle vision? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. Lane markings help a vehicle navigate its road position.
This is correct. Recognizing road users supports safer driving decisions.
This is correct. Road signs provide navigation-relevant visual information.
This is incorrect. Missing-component inspection is a manufacturing quality-control task.
options.better_fit: Manufacturing defect detection fits products moving along an assembly line.

feedback.intrinsic: The selected solution would not address road-safety decisions.
feedback.instructional: Choose capabilities that interpret road conditions and road users.

exercises.explanation: Correct—these capabilities directly support safe navigation decisions.

exercises.question_text: A retail operations lead wants to improve customer experience by finding products placed on the wrong shelf. Which solution best fits?

options.rationale: This is correct. It detects misplaced products and supports shelf availability.
This is incorrect. It examines factory products for defects and missing components.
options.better_fit: Manufacturing defect detection fits assembly-line quality control.

feedback.intrinsic: Shoppers could still encounter misplaced products.
feedback.instructional: The decision concerns store-shelf placement, which fits retail shelf monitoring.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. It supports recognition and decisions in road environments.
options.better_fit: Autonomous vehicle vision fits road signs, lanes, pedestrians, and vehicles.

feedback.instructional: Road navigation does not monitor store shelves.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. It assists with interpretation of patient scans.
options.better_fit: Medical imaging analysis fits radiology scan review.

feedback.intrinsic: The operations issue would remain unresolved.
feedback.instructional: Choose the solution whose camera task is stock and product placement.

exercises.explanation: Correct—retail shelf monitoring is designed to find misplaced shelf products.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The relationship between the tool and scan review becomes unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name the capability first, then who it helps, followed by the scan types.

exercises.correct_answer: Computer vision can help radiologists analyze X-rays, MRIs, and CT scans.
exercises.explanation: Computer vision assists radiologists with analysis of medical scans.

exercises.question_text: Inspecting assembly-line products for surface defects is manufacturing defect ___.

parts.text: Inspecting assembly-line products for surface defects is manufacturing defect

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The factory task would be assigned to the wrong use case.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use this term for visual quality checks on manufactured products.

exercises.explanation: Manufacturing defect detection inspects assembly-line products for defects.

exercises.question_text: A hospital manager is selecting a vision solution to assist radiologists reviewing X-rays. Which reasons justify choosing medical imaging analysis? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. Highlighting anomalies directly supports X-ray review.
This is correct. Assistance with image review can reduce human error.
This is incorrect. Out-of-stock detection is a retail shelf-monitoring use.
options.better_fit: Retail shelf monitoring fits camera-based monitoring of store shelves.

feedback.intrinsic: The X-ray review requirement would not be met.
feedback.instructional: Choose benefits tied to assisting radiologists with medical scans.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. Lane recognition supports vehicle navigation.
options.better_fit: Autonomous vehicle vision fits road-environment interpretation.

feedback.intrinsic: The selected system would not help interpret X-rays.
feedback.instructional: Evaluate options against the hospital's radiology objective.

exercises.explanation: Correct—these benefits directly support radiology review.

exercises.question_text: A production lead wants to reduce waste by stopping products with missing components before shipping. Which solution best fits this decision?

options.rationale: This is correct. It detects missing components during assembly-line inspection.
This is incorrect. It highlights possible anomalies in medical scans.
options.better_fit: Medical imaging analysis fits assisting radiologists with patient images.

feedback.intrinsic: Defective products could still be shipped.
feedback.instructional: The decision concerns product quality and waste reduction on an assembly line.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. It supports road navigation decisions.
options.better_fit: Autonomous vehicle vision fits recognizing road signs, lanes, and people.

feedback.intrinsic: Missing product parts would remain uninspected.
feedback.instructional: Road recognition does not perform factory quality control.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. It detects store stock and shelf-placement issues.
options.better_fit: Retail shelf monitoring fits store inventory checks.

feedback.intrinsic: The shipping-quality decision would lack defect evidence.
feedback.instructional: Select the use case designed to inspect manufactured products.

exercises.explanation: Correct—this solution directly reduces waste from defective products.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the pieces to form a correct statement about segmentation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The definition of segmentation becomes unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the capability, then state what it divides and why.

exercises.correct_answer: Image segmentation divides an image into meaningful regions for detailed analysis.
exercises.explanation: Segmentation divides an image into meaningful regions for closer analysis.
